bead.title: Preserve Kafka identity and offset monotonicity
bead.description:
PROBLEM: Crash and failover re-emission must preserve logical record identity and never move broker offsets backward.
ROOT CAUSE: `docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-008-queue-history-change-records.md:54` through `docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-008-queue-history-change-records.md:60` and `docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-008-queue-history-change-records.md:143` through `docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-008-queue-history-change-records.md:147` define stable identity and monotonic offsets, but `crates/pqueue-engine/src/command.rs:564` through `crates/pqueue-engine/src/command.rs:592` only define the engine-level idempotency key and `crates/pqueue-engine/src/compose.rs:918` through `crates/pqueue-engine/src/compose.rs:951` advance a backend emission cursor without any Kafka offset contract at the embedded surface.
PROPOSED FIX: Carry the canonical record key through fjord emission, persist the per-stream offset advance only after successful delivery, and prove failover replay keeps the logical key stable while offsets move forward.
NON-SCOPE: Dependency pinning, ACL scoping, and consumer-group ownership are handled by sibling beads.
bead.acceptance:
1. `TestKafkaIdempotencyKeyIsStableAcrossReemit` proves the emitted identity stays stable across re-emission.
2. `TestKafkaOffsetNeverRegressesAcrossFailover` proves failover replay does not regress the broker offset stream.
3. `go test ./... -run 'TestKafkaIdempotencyKeyIsStableAcrossReemit|TestKafkaOffsetNeverRegressesAcrossFailover'`
4. `lefthook run pre-commit`
5. `lefthook run pre-push`
